outcome.technical: MED-1, audit-task.py: _own_work_paths now releases a path only when every other declarer holding it has a task tree of its own. That means _tree_resident (re-added): a linked worktree other than the one the start reads, whose marker names the task, read with _worktrees.read_provenance(expect_task); a git listing that will not answer means nobody counts. The window check then still applies. The premise is stated in the docstring and in verbs-in-full.md: a task writes only in the tree its work lives in, and only while it runs. Status does not hold that in a shared checkout, so a declarer with no tree, or with its marker on the start's own tree, is never released. The release line names the tree. LOW-1: _ran_within answers None (can't tell) when an event's `from` is not the previous event's `to`. MED, commit-task-work.py: _commit_work refuses a task whose status is pending, blocked or cancelled before anything is staged, naming the status and pointing to start or --state. `done` is let through. It is the older close order (status before commit); the shared builder test__invariants.build still writes it, and 88 ctw cases depend on it, measured by a full-suite run with a strict in_progress-only guard. Refusing it is caught by the new ctw-at17 (row D5). --state is untouched. A new UNDATED_SHARED refusal covers a declared path that attribute() cannot date (no start record and no startedAt) when another started, unfinished task (_declarers) also declares it; it names that task with ways_past. Tests: P1.2 now has a marked task tree in the shared journal history.
